loveBombing.q1a: Not yet, or after several months, once you knew each other well.
loveBombing.q1b: After a few weeks, and it matched what you were living.
loveBombing.q1c: After two or three weeks, before you really knew each other.
loveBombing.q1d: In the first few days, sometimes before your first date.
loveBombing.q2: Words like "soulmate", "meant to be", "I've never felt this way", you hear them…
loveBombing.q2b: Once or twice, in a tender moment.
loveBombing.q2c: Often, and from the first few weeks.
loveBombing.q2d: All the time: "you're the love of my life", "it was written".
loveBombing.q3: What do the texts look like, day to day?
loveBombing.q3a: A few a day, and nobody worries if you reply later.
loveBombing.q3b: Lots of texts, but a late reply is no problem at all.
loveBombing.q3c: Morning to night, with follow-ups when you don't answer fast.
loveBombing.q3d: Dozens a day, and an hour without a reply starts a scene: "are you ignoring me?", "who were you with?".
loveBombing.q4a: Normal for where you are: a dinner, a book, a small thoughtful thing.
loveBombing.q4b: A bit more than you expected, nothing awkward.
loveBombing.q4c: Often too big for the stage you're at, to the point you don't quite know what to do with them.
loveBombing.q4d: Over the top: expensive jewellery, a trip booked without asking you, and you feel like you owe them.
loveBombing.q5: Moving in, a trip, a baby, getting married: these plans…
loveBombing.q5a: Come up little by little, at the pace of the relationship.
loveBombing.q5b: Already come up a bit, as daydreams, nothing decided.
loveBombing.q5c: Came up very early, and your wish to wait hasn't gone down well.
loveBombing.q5d: Came up within a few weeks, with a date attached, and your "it's too soon" was taken very badly.
loveBombing.q6: When this person talks about you…
loveBombing.q6a: They see you as you are, flaws included, and it makes them smile.
loveBombing.q6b: They think you're amazing, the way people in love do.
loveBombing.q6c: They describe someone perfect, someone you don't quite recognise.
loveBombing.q6d: "You're perfect", "you're not like the others", and you dread the day this person sees the rest.
loveBombing.q7: And their exes, what does this person say about them?
loveBombing.q7a: Not much, or good things about at least some of them.
loveBombing.q7b: One relationship ended badly, as happens.
loveBombing.q7c: Most of them treated this person badly, and you're not like them.
loveBombing.q7d: All crazy, toxic or manipulative, and it was always their fault.
loveBombing.q8: You say no to something ordinary: a night when you're tired, a weekend planned with friends. How does this person react?
loveBombing.q8a: "Ok, no problem", and you both move on.
loveBombing.q8b: A bit of disappointment, said simply, then it passes.
loveBombing.q8c: Pushing or guilt-tripping, until you give in, or almost.
loveBombing.q8d: Sulking, anger or hours of silence: you understand that your no came with a price.
loveBombing.q9: When you slow things down a little (fewer texts, fewer evenings together), this person…
loveBombing.q9a: Follows your pace, even if it's a bit disappointing.
loveBombing.q9b: Asks if everything's okay, then adapts.
loveBombing.q9c: Piles it on: even more texts, gifts, declarations.
loveBombing.q9d: Shows up unannounced, at your place or at work, calls again and again, until you come back just to make it stop.
loveBombing.q10: When you see your friends or family without this person…
loveBombing.q10a: They think it's normal, they have their own life too.
loveBombing.q10b: They tell you they missed you, nothing more.
loveBombing.q10c: They text you all evening, or sulk when you get back.
loveBombing.q10d: You feel guilty before you even go, and you often end up cancelling to keep the peace.
loveBombing.q11: What this person says about the people close to you…
loveBombing.q11a: They like them, or at least stay polite with them.
loveBombing.q11b: They don't click with some of them, as happens.
loveBombing.q11c: They criticise them often: they're jealous, they don't want you to be happy, they're getting in your head.
loveBombing.q11d: They've already made you choose, one way or another, between your loved ones and this relationship.
loveBombing.q12: Does this person want to know where you are and who you're with?
loveBombing.q12a: No, or only to plan things.
loveBombing.q12b: Now and then, out of curiosity.
loveBombing.q12c: Yes: where you are, who with, and what time you'll be home.
loveBombing.q12d: To the point of asking you to share your location, or checking your social media to see what you're up to.
loveBombing.q13: How does this person present their jealousy?
loveBombing.q13a: They barely show any, or laugh about it with you.
loveBombing.q13b: As a little pang now and then, which they admit.
loveBombing.q13c: As proof of love: "it's because I care about you".
loveBombing.q13d: As love, while blaming you for a glance, a colleague, a message.
loveBombing.q14: Since the start of your relationship, the intensity…
loveBombing.q14a: Has calmed down a bit, like in every relationship, and that suits you fine.
loveBombing.q14b: Goes up and down: some very intense weeks, some calmer ones.
loveBombing.q14c: Dropped all of a sudden, and you don't know what you did.
loveBombing.q14d: Has nothing to do with the start: it's not the same person any more, and you spend your time trying to get back the one from the beginning.
loveBombing.q15a: Are still there, less spectacular, and that's normal.
loveBombing.q15b: Are rarer, but the tenderness is still there.
loveBombing.q15c: Have given way to remarks about the way you dress, talk, do things.
loveBombing.q15d: Have been replaced by contempt, sometimes in front of others, to the point you wonder if you're good enough.
loveBombing.q16: "After everything I've done for you": have you heard that one?
loveBombing.q16b: Once, in a fight, with an apology afterwards.
loveBombing.q16c: Several times, when you didn't agree.
loveBombing.q16d: Often: the gifts and gestures of the beginning get thrown back at you as soon as you say no.
loveBombing.q17: After a fight or a few cold days, what happens?
loveBombing.q17a: You talk about it, you both apologise if needed, and things move on.
loveBombing.q17b: A gesture to make up for it: a message, something thoughtful.
loveBombing.q17c: A big comeback, like at the start: flowers, declarations, "I'll change".
loveBombing.q17d: Always the same loop: cold, then an avalanche of love, then cold again, and you hold on thanks to the good moments.
loveBombing.q18b: In love, and sometimes a little overwhelmed by the speed.
loveBombing.q18c: Often anxious, watching their mood or waiting for their next text.
loveBombing.q18d: Like someone else: you've changed your habits, your nights out, the way you talk, to avoid trouble.
loveBombing.q19: Do you ever feel afraid of how this person will react?
loveBombing.q19b: Not afraid, more like not wanting to upset them.
loveBombing.q19c: Sometimes: you think twice before saying certain things.
loveBombing.q19d: Often: you're afraid of what they might say, do or break.
loveBombing.q20: And the people close to you, what do they think?
loveBombing.q20a: They like this person, or they're happy for you.
loveBombing.q20b: They don't know this person well enough yet to have an opinion.
loveBombing.q20c: Some think it's moving very fast, and tell you so.
loveBombing.q20d: Several of them are worried about you, or you see them a lot less than before.
loveBombing.r1_t: An intense start, no love bombing
loveBombing.r1_d: Your answers don't look like love bombing. This person may be very much in love, and it shows, but they respect your pace, they take a no without making a drama of it, and you feel like yourself around them. That's exactly what separates falling hard from being manipulated.
loveBombing.r1_a: Enjoy it! And if a friend told you "this is moving fast", you can reassure them: speed alone means nothing, what counts is how your limits are received, and here that's fine. If something changes in a few months, you know where to find the test.
loveBombing.r2_t: A few signs to keep an eye on
loveBombing.r2_d: Nothing serious in your answers, but two or three things are worth a look: a slightly fast pace, lots of texts, plans that come early. Taken one by one, you see these in plenty of new relationships. What will make the difference is what happens when you say no.
loveBombing.r2_a: Try the limit test: next time, say no to something ordinary, an evening or a late call, and watch the reaction. An "ok, no problem" will reassure you far more than any online test. And if the pace still hasn't slowed in a few weeks, take this one again.
loveBombing.r3_d: Your answers look like love bombing: a lot, very fast, and something that jams as soon as you want to slow down or say no. That doesn't mean this person is doing it on purpose. But this is how the love bombing cycle starts: you're showered with attention so you get attached fast, before you've had time to really know who you're dealing with.
loveBombing.r3_a: Slow down, even if it feels good. Keep your evenings with your friends, don't jump into big plans yet, and watch how this person reacts. And tell someone who knows you well what you're going through: from the outside, this kind of start is much easier to see.
loveBombing.r4_d: Your answers describe more than a start that's too fast. Saying no costs you, the people close to you have become a reason to fight, or you think before you speak to avoid a reaction. That's the love bombing pattern: you're showered with attention at the start so you get attached, then that attention is taken back the moment you do something that isn't liked.
loveBombing.r4_a: What you feel isn't weakness, it's the mechanism at work. Take back what belongs to you: your friends, your evenings, your decisions. Write down what happens, with dates, so you don't start doubting your own memory. And if saying no scares you, talk to someone you trust or to a professional.
loveBombing.r5_t: Love bombing and control: protect yourself
loveBombing.r5_d: What you describe goes beyond love bombing. Your limits aren't respected any more, your life is shrinking around this person, or you're afraid of how they'll react, sometimes all of it at once. At this point it's not a start that's moving too fast, it's a controlling relationship. And it's not your fault.
loveBombing.r5_a: Don't stay alone with this today. In the UK, the National Domestic Abuse Helpline (0808 2000 247) answers for free, 24 hours a day; in the US, the National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233. In immediate danger, call 999 or 911. Tell someone you trust what you're going through, even if you haven't decided anything yet. What you feel is not an exaggeration.
